title: Predicting Long-term Dynamics of Complex Networks via Identifying Skeleton in Hyperbolic Space

problem.claim: Predicting long-term dynamics in complex networks is important for understanding, modeling, and controlling real-world complex systems.

gap.claim: Existing approaches have limited ability to capture long-term dynamics because they overlook the role of inherent low-dimensional network manifolds, or skeletons.

contributions.claim: DiskNet identifies complex-network skeletons in hyperbolic space using a renormalization group structure while preserving topological and dynamics properties.
DiskNet condenses networks with varied dynamics into skeletons through physics-informed hyperbolic embeddings and models condensed dynamics with graph neural ordinary differential equations.
DiskNet reconstructs the original networks and dynamics from the skeletons using a degree-based super-resolution module.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments covering three representative dynamics, five real-world networks, and two synthetic networks.
The authors report that DiskNet outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by an average of 10.18% in long-term prediction accuracy.
The authors state that reproduction code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-term network-dynamics prediction supports understanding, modeling, and control of complex systems.
Current methods have limited long-term predictive capability because they overlook low-dimensional network skeletons.
DiskNet identifies dynamics-preserving network skeletons through renormalization-group structure in hyperbolic space.

The approach embeds and condenses networks, models skeleton dynamics with graph neural ordinary differential equations, and uses degree-based super-resolution to recover the original networks and dynamics.
The authors report superior performance across multiple dynamics and network datasets, including an average 10.18% improvement over state-of-the-art baselines in long-term prediction accuracy.

unknowns: Exact benchmark datasets, baselines, metrics, and experimental settings are not specified.
The abstract does not provide details of the renormalization group construction, hyperbolic embeddings, graph neural ordinary differential equations, or super-resolution module.
The abstract does not report absolute accuracy values, variance, statistical testing, or ablation results.
